newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on technical buying.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on technical buying.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures rose on Thursday, as technical buying emerged following a sharp fall on Wednesday, traders said.
Prices ranged from 140 to 170 yen higher, with the benchmark July 1998 contract ending 170 yen higher at 13,120 yen per tonne. Volume was estimated at 56,885 lots.

On Wednesday, the yen-based corn futures market plunged, with all contracts falling by their daily limits of 400 yen, as the yen's firmer tone against the dollar and the weak Chicago market triggered heavy selling.
"Investors thought the market's plunge yesterday was overdone. Technical buying supported the market from the opening," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.45-3/4 per bushel at 0815 GMT, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $7.12 a bushel at 0815 GMT, against $7.11 at Wednesday's close.
